correctness.rationale: The circle angle-derivative numerator is a concave quadratic with positive endpoint factorizations for 0<k<1/4 and sufficiently small epsilon; Radó–Kneser–Choquet and the positive real-affine Jacobian prove the normalized convex ellipse map. Partial fractions yield exact coefficient tails and local uniform rational self-convolution derivatives. The boundary Jacobian polynomial for the limiting map has positive nonconstant coefficients in y² and constant (6d−1)(6d²+6d−1)/16; with zero-free p’ and the maximum-modulus principle this proves positivity exactly up to d_c, and the negative real-radius factorization proves failure above. Exact Fraction replay confirms the finite ratio <13/10 and negative-Jacobian witness. Critical scope excludes finite-epsilon positivity below threshold.

value.rationale: The natural geometric parameter in the 2026 bounded-ellipse counterexample is its eccentricity. A full if-and-only-if transition in the singular normalized convolution model explains exactly when local orientation fails and supplies bounded convex ellipse counterexamples with arbitrarily small excess above sqrt(5/3), versus the primary source’s displayed axis ratio about 1.32264. The explicit rational example below 1.3 is a reproducible quantitative improvement, but value chiefly comes from the sharp structural phase transition, not from a tiny numeric gain. No universal ellipse threshold is claimed.
